About Malaysia Overview

MBBS in Malaysia

Malaysia is a vibrant Southeast Asian country renowned for its multicultural legacy, modern infrastructure, and high-quality education system. It is home to some of the best medical colleges in Malaysia, making it a top choice for foreign students wishing to study medicine there.

The country boasts a combination of both urban and natural landscapes, from cities such as Kuala Lumpur to natural beauty such as Langkawi. Malaysia, as a stable economy with good healthcare facilities and a high focus on education, has become a top choice for higher education with a low cost of living, making it highly affordable for students.

It is easy to live in Malaysia as a medical student because of friendly student policies, a decent public transportation system, and a welcoming environment. The most widely spoken language is English, especially in educational institutions, making it easy for foreign students to adjust to its safe environment and quality education system.

All Requirements for MBBS in Malaysia

Understand the essential criteria and requirements

Ensure your eligibility for pursuing MBBS and starting your medical journey.

Eligibility Criteria to Apply

To be considered for MBBS admission in Malaysia, candidates must meet the following criteria:

  • Academic Requirement: At least 50% in PCB (Physics, Chemistry, Biology) in 12th standard.
  • NEET Qualification: Mandatory for Indian students by NMC-recognized Malaysian medical colleges.
  • Age Requirement: Must be at least 17 years as of the admission date.
  • English Proficiency: International students have to meet some universities’ requirements with IELTS/TOEFL.

Required Documents & Intake

MBBS admission in Malaysia follows a planned system with two major intakes:

  • March/April Intake: The principal intake for most medical schools.
  • September/October Intake: A secondary intake offering flexibility.

Documents Needed:

10th and 12th-grade mark sheets, NEET scorecard (for Indians), Valid Passport (6 months min), Passport Size Photos, Medical Fitness Certificate, Sponsorship letters or bank statements.

The cost of MBBS in Malaysia is low compared to the West and private medical colleges in India. The cost ranges from INR 25-50 lakhs for the entire course, depending on the university and whether the university is a private medical college in Malaysia or a government university.

Apart from tuition fees, students also need to consider other charges such as accommodation, food, and transport. Living in Malaysia as a medical student has an approximate monthly expense of INR 15,000-25,000. Overall, MBBS admission in Malaysia offers quality education at a low price.

Food, Accommodation & Travel

Comfortable Student Living Rent varies from INR 15,000 to 30,000 per month.

It is comfortable and inexpensive to live in Malaysia, particularly for Indian students. Accommodation types include university hostels, shared apartments, and private accommodations.

Indian students can avail themselves of a multitude of Indian restaurants and supermarkets that offer familiar ingredients. Food expenses are, on average, between INR 8,000 to 15,000 per month. Malaysia also has a very efficient transportation system comprising buses, trains, and taxi services like Grab. The average monthly traveling expenses range from INR 3,000 to 6,000, aided by discounted fares using the MyRapid Card.

Pathway Particulars

Duration of MBBS Course

The MBBS programs in Malaysia typically take 5 to 6 years, consisting of two principal phases: The Pre-Clinical Phase (2 Years) focusing on theoretical studies like anatomy, physiology, and biochemistry. The Clinical Phase (Years 3-4/5) provides practical experience with direct hands-on experience in affiliated hospitals.

Medium of Teaching

The Medium of teaching MBBS in Malaysia is English. It is extensively engaged in medical colleges to be utilized in lectures, books, and examinations. Certain institutions also offer additional language support. It is simple for students to understand medical concepts and communicate effectively with an English-based curriculum.

MBBS Admission In Malaysia

A step-by-step roadmap to admission

  1. Fill out the application form: Fill out the application form/admission from the official website.
  2. Select your University: Select your NMC-approved desired university to study MBBS in Malaysia.
  3. Submit Documents: Submit scanned documents: 10th and 12th mark sheets, NEET score card, copy of the medical certificate, and passport.
  4. Receive Invitation: After 10-15 days of applying and submitting the application form, you’ll get the invitation letter from the university.
  5. Apply for Visa: Students can apply for a visa at the respective embassy, processing typically takes about 10 days.

Scholarships Offered for MBBS in Malaysia

It's not very costly to study MBBS in Malaysia, and various institutions provide scholarships to international students.

  • University-Based: Monash University Malaysia Scholarships and International Medical University Scholarships offer partial or full fee coverage based on merit.
  • Government Scholarships: Malaysia International Scholarship (MIS) and JPA Scholarship awarded to high-achieving students.
  • Private Organizations: Khazanah Global Scholarship and Asian Development Bank Scholarship support students from developing countries.

Career Opportunities After MBBS

Having a globally accepted degree, career prospects following MBBS in Malaysia are vast, with excellent job opportunities.

  • Practice in Malaysia: Graduates can practice after completing the required internship and obtaining a license from the MMC.
  • Practice in India: Indian students can pass the FMGE/NExT exam to practice in India after graduating from an NMC-approved college.
  • Specialization: Study MD/MS abroad or locally in cardiology, neurology, etc.
  • Hospital Administration: Move into hospital management, medical tourism, or health consultancy.
Medical Courses in Malaysia

Comprehensive healthcare programs

Malaysia offers a variety of medical and healthcare-related courses to pursue a medical career globally.

MBBS (Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery)

The most desired course in medical schools of Malaysia, preparing students for general medical practice and specializations.

Dentistry (BDS)

Specialist programs focusing on oral health and comprehensive dental surgery.

Pharmacy (BPharm)

It involves comprehensive training in drug development, dispensing, and advanced patient care.

Nursing and Allied Health Sciences

Includes core disciplines like nursing, physiotherapy, and medical laboratory technology.

Comparing MBBS in Malaysia Vs MBBS in India

Side-by-side decision matrix

01

MBBS in India

  • Cost: High fees in private colleges (up to INR 80 lakh per year), lower in government colleges.
  • Admission process: Competitive NEET exam required for limited government seats; high competition for private seats.
  • Global recognition: Degrees recognized globally but require FMGE/NExT for foreign graduates to practice in India.
  • Language: Primarily taught in English, but regional languages may be used in some institutions.
  • Cultural diversity: Less international diversity compared to Malaysia.
  • Safety & Infrastructure: Safety varies regionally; infrastructure is generally good but can differ between institutions.
  • Clinical training: Clinical training available but may vary in quality between institutions.
02

MBBS in Malaysia

  • Cost: Affordable tuition fees (INR 10-60 lakh for the entire course) and living expenses (INR 20K-30K per month).
  • Admission process: Straightforward admission without entrance exams (except NEET for Indian students).
  • Global recognition: Degrees recognized by WHO, MCI (NMC), and other international bodies.
  • Language: English-medium programs, reducing language barriers for international students.
  • Cultural diversity: Offers a diverse cultural environment, enhancing interpersonal skills.
  • Safety & Infrastructure: Known for political stability and high student safety with excellent facilities.
  • Clinical training: Extensive clinical training opportunities in affiliated hospitals.
